sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factor scores: GOV4, MOAT3, REV1, DUR5, CAP3, CASH2, BAL3, EXEC3, EARN3, RNS, D2, PNS, LNS. Each factor has two supporting facts, contrary evidence, a definition, confidence and cited evidence. REV’s schedule starts at 1 for the preselected negative comparable CAGR; no discretionary uplift is applied. Four comparable years cap historical factors at 8, but none approaches that ceiling. [S01][S02]

BQS =0.20×4+0.20×3+0.12×1+0.10×5+0.12×3+0.10×2+0.08×3+0.08×3 =3.06, displayed 3.1. GQS =0.40×1+0.20×5+0.15×3+0.15×3+0.10×2 =2.50, displayed 2.5. Persistent weak CAP and CASH trigger the explicit GQScap 5, which is nonbinding. There is no governance override because GOV is 4 and G1 has not failed; no undisclosed haircut is applied.

IAS known contribution is 0.25×3.06+0.20×2=1.165. R, P and L omit 55% ofweight, so coverage is 45%; missing-factor bounds are 1.715–6.665, not an estimated score or confidence interval. No renormalization or midpoint is used. The exact unrounded BQS feeds IAS. G2 independently blocks favorable ranking even though descriptive quality scores are numerically computable. One-decimal displays use Decimal HALF_UP; JSON retains exact strings.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The economic core is resin-impregnated decorative paper pressed into laminates at Bareilly, sold largely B2 B through distributors/dealers. Management describes more than 1,000 SKUs and approximately 50 distributors/7,000 retailers. Designs, sizes and surface finishes provide commercial differentiation, but branding alone does not establish retention or price power. Capacity is 5 million sheets with four presses; industrial-laminate capacity is reported separately in kilograms, so those utilization figures cannot be added to sheet volumes. [S01][S02]

FY26 manufactured revenue ₹87.2923 crore, traded goods ₹16.3172 crore and scrap ₹0.6693 crore sum to ₹104.2788 crore. Manufacture was 83.71% ofrevenue and trading 15.65%, versus 89.08%/10.22% in FY25. Plywood production was curtailed because dust affected laminates; branded external plywood and veneer then replaced some manufacture. This is a lower-value-add mix change, not necessarily lost branded plywood sales: total plywood sales rose during FY23–25 even while manufactured plywood dropped. Management’s 15–30% manufacturing versus 6–11% trading gross-margin ranges are not audited segment contribution margins. [S01][S02]

Materials-only value addition was ₹32.6750 crore in FY26, before labour, power, conversion costs and distribution. It is deliberately not called gross profit. Cash costs include kraft/decor paper, phenol/melamine and power; supplier and customer credit are central economics. Revenue is recognized on delivery, with 30–180 day stated terms. The business reports a single operating segment, so reliable product-level EBIT, unit contribution and acquired-depot profit are ND. [S01]

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
A defensible moat would require persistent realization premiums after quality/thickness mix, superior cost per comparable sheet, resilient collections, distributor retention or demonstrable switching costs. None is sufficiently established. FY25 laminate production fell 9.57% while laminate revenue fell 2.18%. The resulting 8.17% rise in revenue per produced sheet is only a proxy: stock movement, shipment timing and mix separate production from units sold. It is not a verified ASP increase. [S02]

Relevant peers are economic reference points, not transplanted P/Es. Greenlam’s FY25 laminate segment had ₹2,226.37 crore revenue and ₹369.10 crore EBIT, reflecting much larger geographic/product scale. Stylam’s May 2026 presentation describes 20 million-sheet capacity, approximately 74% utilization, net-debt-free status and export-heavy shipments; those are management disclosures, not independently copied valuation multiples. Rushil is a weaker comparator: FY26 laminate revenue ₹214.421 crore and EBIT ₹13.913 crore, against ₹201.774 crore/₹19.465 crore in FY25, showing that volume growth need not preserve margins. Rushil’s MDF group exposure is not treated as directly comparable. [S15][S16][S17]

Manilam’s distributor reach, existing plant and design breadth are useful assets. Against them stand commodity-input exposure, concentrated channel economics, falling utilization and modest cash returns. MOAT3 reflects this balance. No monopoly, patented technology, high switching cost or industry market-share gain is inferred from catalogue breadth or an IPO-sponsored industry forecast.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
The scoring window was selected before scoring: FY23–FY26, the four comparable Ind AS observations. Revenue ₹148.1016→₹137.8954→₹140.0266→₹104.2788 crore gives a three-year CAGR of-11.04%. Manufactured revenue fell from ₹140.3685 crore to ₹87.2923 crore, CAGR-14.64%. The five-year ₹70.0539 crore FY21 base gives 8.28% headlinegrowth but combines pandemic recovery and accounting changes; it is not chosen to disguise the subsequent contraction. [S01][S02][S06]

Laminate production 4.237 m→4.053 m→3.665 m sheets in FY23–25 corresponds to 84.74%,81.07%,73.31% utilization. H1 FY26 production 1.208 m was only 48.30% annualized utilization; industrial laminates remain a different-unit, small-utilization line. FY26 full-year shipment volume/ASP and product-level mix are unavailable. We therefore cannot split the latest decline numerically into unit volume, pricing and mix. [S02]

FY26 trading grew 14.04% while manufacture contracted 30.02%; gross growth would increasingly reflect purchased product value rather than plant productivity. The promoter-related Bangalore depot takeover introduces an acquired-distribution component whose sales and profit are not isolated. The precise organic growth rate is ND, but declining core manufacturing does not support a high REV score. H1 FY26 revenue ₹60.2623 crore/PAT ₹3.2117 crore versus full-year ₹104.2788 crore/₹2.0591 crore implies a weaker H2 residual, not an extrapolated FY27 forecast. No matched current/prior half-year recovery series exists.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The incremental return bridge separates profits from their financing. Operating EBIT excludes all other income; normalized NOPAT uses 30% tax. FY23 NOPAT ₹4.7026 crore to FY26₹6.20109 crore adds ₹1.49849 crore. Funded capital, defined as equity+debt+leases−allcash−non-operating investment, rises ₹83.9659 crore to ₹112.3018 crore, adding ₹28.3359 crore. Incremental return is 5.29%, below an illustrative 12–16% capital-costrange. A core operating-net-assets denominator gives 4.57%, so the weak result is not created by one net-debt definition. [S01][S02]

The financing bridge is exact: equity+₹47.2795 crore, debt−₹9.8459 crore, cash+₹9.6677 crore and lease debt+₹0.57 crore yield the ₹28.3359 crore change. FY24–26 cash capex totals ₹3.2399 crore against ₹8.2465 crore depreciation. Most added capital therefore sits in working assets rather than a demonstrably productive new fixed-asset cohort. Depreciation is not a maintenance-capex forecast; the forward model retains 2.7% ofsales maintenance and tests 1.5–4%. [S01][S02]

This is an aggregate shareholder-capital attribution, not a precise pure-organic project IRR. The acquired depot transfers receivables, inventory, deposits and advances, partly settling a promoter balance; no separate acquired EBIT is disclosed. We do not call the ₹9.5726 crore asset basket cash capex or grant it goodwill/property value. Available plant capacity and IPO-funded ₹1.25 crore equipment/₹2.20 crore solar could improve unit economics, but favorable CAP requires observed incremental contribution and collections, not an unused-capacity narrative. CAP3 and GQS2.5 reflect the demonstrated record.

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 61.93% at 31 March 2026, with no reported pledge, warrants, convertibles or outstanding ESOPs. Total locked-in shares were 77.25%; public 38.07% is not equivalent to readily tradable free float. The ₹7.5348 crore IPO offer-for-sale paid selling holders, not the company; the ₹6 crore pre-IPO placement and ₹32.4162 crore fresh IPO were company financing. Commercial RPTs and seller liquidity alone are not proof of abuse. [S01][S02][S11][S12]

However, outside related receivables of ₹6.0813 crore and asset-based settlement require a clear arm’s-length bridge. FY26 purchases from related entities are substantial. Two managing directors received ₹1.44 crore salary, about 70% of PAT; three principal executives together ₹1.80 crore, about 87%. Auditor reporting states remuneration complied with applicable provisions, so this is an alignment/economic issue rather than an allegation of illegality. [S01]

Execution is mixed: the IPO closed and bank term borrowing fell, but production, utilization and manufactured sales weakened. FY25 PFdues ₹5.55 lakhwere older than six months; FY26 CAROreports no equivalent aged undisputed arrears. Old land deeds remain in the converted partnership’s name; conversion context is explicit. July 2026 director resignations cite travel/time constraints and professional priorities; the company secretary cited personal reasons. A replacement was not located in the reviewed cutoff disclosures. These are monitoring items, not invented hidden disputes. Board oversight and independent confirmations need to demonstrate that finance discipline matches the newly listed-company obligations. [S01][S02][S13][S14]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Full main audit, standalone CARO, consolidated CARO applicability, IFC, secretarial audit and audit-trail statements were reviewed, not just the clean opinion. FY26 audit reports no material bank-return discrepancy, no fraud/default identified, effective holding-company IFC and operating untampered audit trail. Emphases nevertheless retain unconfirmed/reconciliation-sensitive trade balances and incomplete MSME identification. The fully impaired Myanmar investment creates no additional book-value deduction here. Historical unprovided gratuity is distinguished from the current recognized provision. [S01–S06]

Receivables ₹63.6525 crore equal about 223 days of FY26 revenue; ₹11.0237 crore is over one year old, with nil ECL. Management cites recoveries and enforceability but gives no sufficiently quantified subsequent-cash schedule. Inventory ₹64.8008 crore includes ₹56.6369 crore finished goods and no slow-moving provision. Payables ₹36.9237 crore include ₹7.3648 crore over one year. These asset-quality uncertainties are material beside ₹70.5235 crore equity. RPT receivables fell ₹14.8770 crore, but acquired current assets and goods mean it is not all cash collection. [S01]

FY23–26 reported CFO totals ₹3.3555 crore against ₹14.2620 crore PAT, conversion 23.53%; after cash capex the cumulative FCF proxy is negative ₹4.9397 crore. Reported finance cost totals ₹25.21 crore and is predominantly financing-classified cash interest; deducting once makes the owner-cash proxy substantially worse. FY24/FY25 statutory-to-prospectus interest timing moves ₹1.1040 crore between years, with virtually no cumulative CFOdifference; we preserve rather than double-count it. [S01][S02][S03]

Note 38 tax contingencies ₹16.1712 crore are disputed, not proven liabilities; stress uses this wider total once, not the sum with CARO. The maturity table’s 1–5 year placement of ₹50.6867 crore conflicts with explicit demand terms for ₹47.4815 crore. Cash-flow closing cash differs from BS by ₹0.0142 crore, and EPS/OCI presentation differences remain open. Small differences alone do not drive G2; the decisive issue is material asset recoverability and cash attribution. Thus G2 Hold coexists with fair acknowledgment of an unmodified audit. [S01]

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the observed 16 October ₹51.25 price, market capitalization is ₹111.971 crore; current-issued-share EPS ₹0.9425 gives 54.38 xreported P/E, not the lower ratio obtained from weighted EPS ₹1.17. Bookvalue ₹32.28/share is not a liquidation floor because aged receivables and inventory require realization. Conventional all-cash net debt is ₹41.2083 crore; excluding ₹9.50 crore earmarks leaves ₹50.7083 crore cash-available net debt. Treating leases as recurring rentals yields approximately ₹162.6793 crore EV and 14.14 xcash-rent EBITDA. No operating land/property value is added to earnings EV. [S01][S09][S10]

The model spans 31 March 2026 to 19 October 2031 with an explicit 19 October 2026 entry breakpoint,1826 holdingdays and ACT/365.25 discounting. IPO funds enter only once at the reported balance date: eligible WC money funds actual modeled purchases, equipment/solar budgets fund dated uses, and OFS is excluded. Old taxes, statutory dues, accrued interest, capital creditors, employee payables and current gratuity are settled once by September; remaining legacy gratuity is deducted once terminally. Cash rentals recur; lease debt is not also deducted. No proposed ₹25 crorefacility or new debt is assumed. [S01][S07][S08]

The 11% cash-EBITDA/7% growthcase first breaches the ₹0.15 crore analyst reserve in October 2028 and needs up to ₹10.15 crore byterminal; ordinary and conditionalnon-rescue IRRs/entry prices are null. Flat growth with 222.8 receivable days (near FY26 actual), 328 inventory-cost days and 187 supplier-cost days is conditionally funded but implies roughly−18.5% annualized return. Bull assumptions 18% first-yearrebound,12% subsequent growth,14.5% cash margin and better collections/inventory yield a funded diagnostic 16.4% return. Its conditional 12/15/18% hurdle entry values are ₹62.07/₹54.39/₹47.82; none is an actionable target while G2/quote constraints remain.

A finite funded bracket shows that 10% growth, improved WC and 8 xexit require approximately 16.60% cash EBITDAmargin to meet 15% at ₹51.25. The sourcecase is closer to 11%, so price requires combined recovery. DCF retains terminal maintenance/growth reinvestment and signed entry cash reserve, tests 13/15/17% WACC separately from 12/15/18% equityhurdles, and never assigns a supported value to an unfinanceable path.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text:
The permanent-loss chain is operational and financial: slow dealer collections plus finished-goods obsolescence consume cash; suppliers shorten terms; fully used demand facilities cannot expand; tax demands or debt calls then force an issue at a discount. The linked bear assumes 15% first-year sales decline,2% later growth,7.5% cash EBITDA,260 receivable days,360 inventory-cost days,140 supplier-cost days,25% tax-demand payment,5% receivablecash loss,10% cash-creditcall and full ₹4.94 crore unsecured call. These are analyst stresses, not forecasts or observed events. [S01][S07][S08]

The pre-receipt checkpoint funds positive working-capital deployment, capex, legacy liabilities, principal and contingent uses before crediting EBITDA or negative working-capital release. Routine operating receipts and costs, interest and current taxes are netted ratably within each interval; daily cash solvency is not established. The flat case passes by only about ₹0.0114 crore above the ₹0.15 crore reserve at its tightest forecast checkpoint. Rounding receivable days from 222.8 to 223 creates a separate unfunded stress case.

The bear first breaches the cash floor in July 2026, before the hypothetical entry date, so there is no non-rescue return even if a later equityraise would fill the hole. A separate explicit rescue issues whole shares at 30% discount to ₹51.25, pays 3% fees and prefunds each interval’s cash needs; gross, fees, net, share expansion and percentage ownership dilution are shown separately. Pre-entry rescues are counterfactual, not reported financing. Despite repair, this severely stressed branch has no positive terminal residual for ordinary equity; limited liability bounds the loss at 100%, not a return below−100%.

Counterevidence matters. There was no reported FY26 default, the Mayrating is BBB−/Stable, A3, and a flat-survival cash case is financeable with facilities continuing and no adverse tax realization. That prevents calling this an evidenced insolvency solely from an ambitious growth case. G3 is Conditional, not Fail. Two-way matrices vary working capital jointly, capex/multiple, reserve/tax demand and WC-release-delay/debt-call. Higher selected reserve can fail at the opening balance; that is explicitly an analyst reserve deficit, not proof the company defaulted. No probability-weighted return blends unfunded branches into a benign mean.

sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
sections.text:
A5 xshare-price outcome over five years needs 37.97% annual compounding;10 xneeds 58.49%. Over ten years the required rates are 17.46% and 25.89%. These are mathematical requirements, not likely outcomes. The small ₹111.97 croremarketcap supplies no automatic advantage if operating cash must repeatedly finance working capital or dilution. [S09][S10]

At the current 21.848 millionshares,5 x and 10 xprices imply equity values ₹559.855 crore and ₹1119.71 crore. With a deliberately illustrative ₹47.48 croreterminal debt and no surpluscash,8 xterminal EV/EBITDA requires roughly ₹75.92 crore/₹145.90 crore EBITDA, versus FY26₹11.76 crore beforecashrent. At 15% cash EBITDAmargin that means approximately ₹506 crore/₹973 crore revenue, several times FY26₹104.28 crore. Neither existing 5 million-sheetcapacity nor new projects’ disclosed budgets establish that expansion path. [S01][S02]

A more generous 10 xmultiple or a debt-freebalance lowers the required operations, but adds a favorable assumption; repeated equity issuance raises the needed enterprise outcome per original share. Manufacture/tradingmix and cash conversion must improve together, and incremental NOPAT currently falls well short of capital cost. The feasibility model therefore treats 5 x/10 xas a scale-and-financing checklist, not an upside-price target, and does not infer an undisclosed capacity plan or permit free terminal growth.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before relying on this dossier for an entry, obtain a quantified cash-collection schedule for receivables, including related parties and the ₹11.02 crore over-one-year bucket; confirmation coverage; an ECL/slow-stock assessment; and a cash-versus-current-assets reconciliation for the promoter-depot settlement. Resolution must be numeric, not a generic statement that all balances are good. Reconcile the maturity table with demand loan terms and the small cash/EPS differences. These are the G2 release conditions. [S01]

Next reporting cycle: check H1 FY27 sales, actual laminate shipments and realized prices by comparable size/thickness; plant utilization; manufactured versus traded product contributions; repeat dealer concentration; and cash conversion after financing costs. A claimed recovery should show at least two matched half-years/fourquarters, not annualization of one seasonal print. Verify solar/equipment commissioning and separately measured savings against recurring maintenance. CAP should improve through incremental profit on all required working/fixed capital, not only a higher current ROCE denominator. [S01][S02]

Funding triggers: verify current unrestricted cash, legal IPO deployment, demand-facility sanction/renewal, unsecured loan terms, actualstatutory payments and the status/amount of appealedtax demands. Receivables/inventorygrowth faster than sales, further agedpayables, new pledges/dilution or changed audit qualification would tighten the view. Conversely, confirmed collections, sustainedcash interest coverage and self-funded maintenance would improve it. [S01][S07][S08]

Implementation: refresh the actual last trade, exact lot, complete 20/60 sessionseries, spreads/depth and exchange restrictions; do not replace missing sessions with zero. ₹5 lakhis only a reference. Review company secretary replacement and stated board-oversight changes on subsequent filings. No orders, external messages, automatic purchases or monitoring commitments are implied by these research triggers. [S09–S14]

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability and implementation; weak demonstrated business/growth quality, not a compounder designation. BQS3.06/GQS2.50 are descriptive and price-insensitive. IAS remains NS because a supported ordinary return and full-window liquidity assessment are not available. G2 excludes favorable rankings even if a conditional model happens to clear 15%. No forced recommendation follows from the framework’s numerical outputs.

The adverse conclusion is not based on the company being recently listed, its small marketcap or its sector alone. Reliable pre-IPOhistory was credited. The reasons are declining core throughput and manufactured revenue, weak aggregate incremental returns, persistent poor cash conversion and material asset recoverability questions. Counterevidence, including clean statutory opinions, no reported default, fresh company capital and the latest investment-grade rating letter, is explicitly retained. [S01][S02][S07]

Reconsider only when the reliability issues are quantitatively resolved, near-current cash/debt facilities are verified, and a conservative self-funded operating case meets the user-selected hurdle at a verifiable executable price. A lower price alone cannot cure G2 or create tradable liquidity. An existing holder would face different liquidity/risk decisions from a new purchaser; no personal holding, risk tolerance or suitable position has been assumed. Do not rank the conditionalbull case beside companies with supported ordinary returns.

Primary evidence comprises five years of statutory material, the final IPO prospectus/restated financials, two rating-agency disclosures, aggregate shareholding/encumbrance records, July management changes, official dated market/security files and three relevant peer sources. The source register records exact URL, document/retrieval date, page/section and original-payload hash where locally retrieved. The readable report uses source IDs beside material facts; the canonical dossier embeds complete historical, funding, scenario and sensitivity rows. Originals are not needed to rerun calculations from the safe financial extracts, but those extracts cannot independently reauthenticate the original documents.

Outstanding facts: exact post-March cash/eligible IPOspend, confirmed receivable collections, acquired-depot organic/profit attribution, FY26 shipment ASP, product-level contribution, detailed current loan renewal terms, tax-appeal outcomes, company-secretary replacement,19 Octoberprice and missing issuer rows/order-book restrictions. ND is not zero. Model working-capitaldays, margins, growth, capital cost, maintenance reinvestment, tax cash loss and rescue terms are analyst assumptions, not company guidance. No proposed facility or optional equity money is treated as received.

Source conflicts are preserved: original GAAP versus restated Ind AS; ₹1.1040 crore interest timing; numerator/denominator issues in prospectus customer percentages; contractual demand terms versus maturity table; cash/EPS/OCIminor differences; and wider tax-note totals versus CARO. Financial analysis is uncertain and is not a guarantee of value, solvency or execution.
